cli_walk.mistakes_note: All ten ran with fetch, sockets and name lookups made to fail; none was attempted. stderr was empty. Every next action shown was a command that exists.
still_had_to_guess: What <origin> means: arrive gives the flag as --origin <origin> and no example. help door and the refusal say a scheme and a host.

Which flag was wrong: INVALID_ARGUMENTS says the arguments do not match the usage and points to help. It does not name the missing or extra flag, so door check without its two required numbers costs a second read.

The Entry ID: the blank entry gives the form (date, short lowercase label, three-digit number) and does not say what the number counts or who picks the label. feedback check says only whether the ID is already in this checkout's notebook.
Where an adoption record is found: door rights reads a local file, and nothing at the door says where a host keeps one. Finding or fetching a record was not built.
That --out wants an absolute path: arrive does not say; help feedback and the refusal do.
Whether to send: door plan says the decision is made outside the kit. That is a choice left to the caller, not a gap in the text; the walk did not send.
